🇰🇵⚠️ Kim Yo Jong’s World Tour of Blame

Kim Yo Jong, a senior North Korean official and the sister of Kim Jong Un, has issued a statement on the world’s major crises. Her conclusion: the United States and its allies are responsible for Ukraine, the Middle East, East Asia, and the general failure of the planet to behave itself.

On Ukraine, Pyongyang says the West provoked the war by trying to impose a “strategic defeat” on Russia. North Korea again gave full backing to Moscow’s war and denied Kyiv’s claims that it plans to send additional troops. Cooperation with Russia, Kim said, is legal, sovereign, and covered by the two countries’ strategic partnership treaty. 

Russia is therefore the victim. Ukraine is the proxy. The West is the cause. North Korea is merely the loyal ally with a treaty and a very large artillery inventory.

Then came Japan.

Kim said North Korea sees Japan’s military buildup as a present and future threat. Pyongyang now treats Japan’s military facilities as potential targets, she said. 

If Tokyo makes the “wrong choice,” it could face an “immediate” and “annihilating” strike. Japan’s rearmament, she added, amounts to carrying brushwood into a fire. 

That is how North Korea describes Japan’s defense policy: not a response to North Korean missiles, nuclear weapons, or repeated strike threats, but an irresponsible attempt to make itself a target of North Korean missiles.

The United States also received its regular citation.

Trump ordered a reduction in the size and duration of joint U.S.-South Korean exercises. Kim said the decision was “not worth commenting on” and that North Korea had no interest in it. A smaller exercise, she argued, remains aggressive if it is still aimed at North Korea. 

She listed this year’s U.S.-South Korean drills anyway: air exercises, naval rescue training, mine warfare exercises, tactical-air drills, logistics training, and Freedom Shield. The point was not that one exercise had been shortened. The point was that the alliance still has an alliance, and Pyongyang considers that an intolerable fact.

Kim also dismissed reports that Trump and Kim Jong Un had recently communicated. She said she knew nothing about it — perhaps, she added, the only matter involving the country’s foreign policy that she did not know.

Yet Kim Jong Un, she said, still has “good memories and feelings” toward Trump. Their personal relationship remains excellent.

The official formula is almost elegant: Trump is remembered warmly; his government is treated as a permanent threat. The leader-to-leader relationship is fine. The nuclear deterrent remains necessary. The joint drills are hostile. Russia is defending itself. Japan is one bad decision away from annihilation.

Pyongyang has solved the contradiction by treating personal sentiment and state policy as two unrelated departments. One handles memories. The other handles missiles.

📡 Iran to revamp defense industry based on recent war experience: Defense Ministry

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Iranian Defense Ministry says it will restructure and modernize the country’s defense industry in line with the experience and lessons learned from recent wars, stressing the need to adapt defense capabilities to emerging requirements.

In a statement issued ahead of National Defense Industry Day on August 22, the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics said on Thursday that Iran’s defense industry has been built on domestic knowledge and capabilities in response to threats and sanctions, and has become one of the pillars of the country’s power and deterrence.
​
The ministry paid tribute to the martyrs of the defense industry and highlighted the role of Iranian scientists, specialists and young people in developing the country’s defense capabilities.
​
The statement said that the recent imposed wars served as a real test of the country’s defense capabilities, adding that the achievements of the defense industry, alongside the capabilities of the Armed Forces and the Iranian people, thwarted a significant part of the enemy’s calculations.
​
The Ministry of Defense stressed that the wars also revealed new requirements as well as existing strengths and weaknesses. Accordingly, it said, the defense industry will be continuously modernized, restructured, and updated in line with the lessons learned from these wars.
​
The statement also emphasized the concept of a “revolution in the defense industry” based on national defense participation, the use of knowledge-based companies’ capabilities, smart technologies, and accelerating the transformation of knowledge into defense capabilities.
​
The ministry reiterated that its main mission is to transform “field experience into knowledge, knowledge into technology, and technology into future defense capabilities”, stressing that achieving this goal requires the participation of universities, specialists, knowledge-based companies and the public.
